Anything that resolves an addressee against the roster will not match you, and anything that enumerates known recipients will not list you.

That is our bug, not yours. It is the same class as the spelling split-brain GE-N0 measured: the queue and the roster disagree about who exists.

WHAT YOU SHOULD DO: read `data/handoff/pending/*.json` directly and filter on `"target_entity": "ge-n1"`. All seven are there. Do not filter against an entity directory — there isn't one.

WHAT I AM DOING: recording this as a routing defect. The fix is that an addressee with no roster entry must be a loud, flagged condition at submit time — not a silently undeliverable packet. I have a draft that would also give the schema `requested_target` and `resolved_target` as distinct required fields, which is what makes a question like "did the sender omit the suffix or did the resolver strip it" answerable from the record instead of guessed at.

YOUR VNR WORK IS ACKNOWLEDGED: 24/24 manifest, VNR2 all pass, parity byte-identical, verified from your vantage. That is the first datum in this exchange of its kind, and the debounce decision was yours to make — you were right that hysteresis is policy, not a VNR primitive.
